title: Comparison of effective phacoemulsification time and corneal endothelial cell loss using three different ultrasound frequencies: A randomized controlled trial

license.statement: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (article <license>); not CC BY, record kept private

indication: Hard senile cataract (LOCS III nuclear colour 5.6-6.9); eyes below the ECD inclusion minimum, with raised IOP, corneal dystrophy or scars, or previous intraocular surgery excluded

groups.description: Phacoemulsification with a 28-kHz sonotrode (Geuder Megatron S4 HPS; 40% US power, cool flash, identical fluidics)
Phacoemulsification with a 42-kHz sonotrode, otherwise identical settings
Phacoemulsification with a 53-kHz sonotrode, otherwise identical settings; the arm the trial was designed to evaluate against the 28- and 42-kHz sonotrodes

notes: Randomized parallel three-arm trial (block randomization, masked participants and outcome assessor), 207 eyes of 207 patients, 69 per arm; two surgeons.

Role assignment: the Introduction states the trial compared a 53-kHz sonotrode with 28- and 42-kHz sonotrodes, and the authors declare a pending sonotrode patent, so the 53-kHz arm is recorded as treated and the 28- and 42-kHz arms as control.
Specular microscopy at 1 week and 1, 3 and 6 months after surgery.
